items.facts: Reddit fell approximately 30% on 2026-10-30, its biggest single-day decline since its 2024 IPO, after third-quarter results disappointed: daily active unique visitors fell short of Wall Street expectations and fourth-quarter revenue guidance came in below analyst forecasts. Beinsure also flags a search-traffic dependency risk (recovery seen as contingent on growing audience/ad revenue with less reliance on Google search) and that Reddit plans to test mandatory logins in select non-U.S. markets in Q4 2026. Shares had already fallen roughly 43% year-to-date before this drop. Broader market recaps (Global Banking & Finance, Alain Guillot) group Reddit with Intel as the session's two biggest 'AI stalwart' casualties.
items.caveat: Beinsure is the only source with Reddit-specific detail found; treated as single-sourced for the specific guidance figures, corroborated only generally (that Reddit fell hard same day as Intel) by the two market-recap pieces.

items.topic: Intel (INTC) -28.58% on 2026-10-30, Q3 beat / weak Q4 guidance
items.facts: Intel beat Q3 2026 estimates (revenue $16.5B, +21% YoY, in line with consensus; adjusted EPS $0.52 vs. ~$0.40 expected) but guided Q4 revenue to $15B-$16B against an LSEG consensus near $17.1B, and adjusted EPS to $0.25 vs. $0.43 consensus. Drivers cited: a deepening PC-market contraction (one source cites a projected ~10% 2027 decline after an ~12% 2026 slide) and an October production disruption at Intel's Israel fab plus a substrate shortage. Shares fell roughly 20-23% after hours on 10-29 and extended to a premarket drop reported at 25-26% on 10-30 (one source: 'worst since 1974'). Cantor Fitzgerald cut its price target to $90 from $125; other coverage cites a Bank of America rating cut.
items.caveat: No tier-one wire (Reuters/CNBC original) located in this search; figures corroborated across five secondary/aggregator outlets which agree on the direction and rough magnitude but differ by 2-3 points on the exact drop size — reported as a range.

items.facts: No dated, named-source reporting specific to AMD's 2026-10-30 move was found despite multiple searches; AMD's last confirmed guidance cycle in these results traces to August 2026 (Q3 guide), not an Oct 29/30 report. General market recaps (hedgeweek, AJC/AP wire via adn.com, STL.News) describe a broad, same-day chip-sector pullback tied to renewed doubts about AI-infrastructure spending sustainability following Intel's and Alphabet's results, without naming AMD specifically.
items.caveat: No company-specific catalyst found for AMD; reported in the brief as such rather than inferred. Read as part of the broad sector move, not an idiosyncratic story.

items.topic: Broad Oct 30 2026 tech/AI-capex-doubt selloff, press framing for Monday Story section
items.facts: AP wire coverage (via adn.com) and hedgeweek describe a global tech rout on 2026-10-30 driven by weak earnings (Intel, Reddit) and renewed doubt about the pace/payoff of AI infrastructure spending, following Alphabet's -12.6% drop (its worst day in two decades, per Thursday 10-29 reporting) on rising capex and negative free cash flow. STL.News (citing Reuters) put the Nasdaq about 7.8% below its October 6 record close by Friday's close. Global Banking & Finance frames the week as led by the biggest AI-buildout spenders (Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, Alphabet) with hyperscaler capex, partly externally funded, adding to investor nervousness.
items.caveat: Index-level percentages differ slightly across outlets (intraday vs. close); this system's own script-computed closes (data/state.json) are used for every number in the brief, these sources are used only for the narrative framing and attribution.
